archetype.name: Pocket Passer (late-career)
archetype.definition: A 42-year-old who wins with timing and placement from the pocket, no longer adds anything as a runner, and depends on quick, defined throws between the numbers more than on extending plays.

report.headline: Short-and-middle passing still works; everything outside and on third down is failing.
report.take:
Rodgers is no longer the player whose 2011, 2014 and 2020 seasons ranked at or near the top of the league in EPA per play. He has settled into a different pocket passer: an operator who wins on rhythm throws and play-action and gets nothing from his legs. He has 7 carries for 12 yards and two scrambles in 168 dropbacks. His EPA per play has sat between 0.041 and 0.064 for three straight seasons, and this year's -0.11 per dropback (32nd of 42) is a step below even that. It is not a four-game blip coming out of nowhere. The accuracy markers have been sliding for a while: a 20.3% bad-throw rate ranks last among 32 charted QBs.

What is new is how he is being used. Pittsburgh passes 6.5 points more than situation predicts, third-most in the league, even though its run game ranks 6th in EPA. His intended air yards have climbed to 8.66 from 6.0 last season, and his aggressiveness rate is up from 14.5% to 17.65%. The deeper diet produces the splashy lines: three deep touchdowns, and 591 yards with six scores in Weeks 3-4. It also produces a 20.7% completion rate on throws of 20+ yards, a -13.9 CPOE there, and two of his four interceptions.

The splits show clearly where he is still good. Throws of 0-9 air yards return +0.255 EPA with a positive CPOE. Throws over the middle return +0.592, with four of his seven touchdowns, and the tight ends and Roman Wilson are his most efficient targets. Under center he is +0.396 per play with zero sacks. From shotgun he is -0.272 with all 13 sacks, and on third down he is -0.453 with 8 of those sacks at an average of 7.3 yards to go. Some of that is selection: shotgun means passing downs and play-action means early downs. Still, it shows what happens once the defense knows a pass is coming. He holds the ball 2.87 seconds, noticeably longer than last year's 2.59, and nearly a third of his pressures become sacks.

The outlook is a quarterback whose box scores will often look better than his efficiency. The volume is baked into the play-calling, and the deep shots will keep producing touchdowns at a rate his completion percentage doesn't really support. The baseline is a below-average passer who is very good in a narrow lane. Facing a defense that can't punish the shotgun-pass downs, he can post a big yardage game. Against a real pass rush, expect another Week 2.

strengths.title: Quick game between the numbers
strengths.body: Throws under 10 air yards and over the middle are the healthy part of his game. He is completing 71% short with positive CPOE, and the middle of the field is producing nearly +0.6 EPA per throw. This is timing and anticipation, which age erodes slowest, so it should hold. The tight ends and Wilson are the main beneficiaries.

strengths.title: Play-action from under center
strengths.body: On 34 under-center dropbacks he is +0.396 EPA with a 53% success rate and no sacks. This is a run game ranked 6th in EPA setting up his throws. The sample is small and the early-down context helps, but it is the clearest structural edge the offense has. It argues for more of it, not less.

strengths.title: Guaranteed volume
strengths.body: Pittsburgh's pass-heavy lean keeps his attempts near 38 a game. With more downfield throws mixed in, he can pile up yardage even when efficiency is poor, as in Weeks 3-4 with 292 and 299 yards. This comes from the play-calling rather than his form, so it should last as long as the staff keeps choosing it.

concerns.title: Accuracy is now a real flaw
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate ranks last among charted QBs and has risen in three of four games, reaching 25.6% last week. CPOE was -6.4 in each of his last two starts despite the big yardage. His bad-throw rate has been in the mid-to-high teens for years, so this is a worsening of an existing problem rather than a blip, and it is unlikely to snap back.

concerns.title: Third down and obvious passing downs
concerns.body: On third down he converts 28.6% with -0.453 EPA, and 8 of his 13 sacks come there. On those downs he lacks the mobility to escape and the arm to fit late throws, and a 32.5% pressure-to-sack rate has tracked his 2024-25 levels. The 18-blitz Week 2 loss (-21.4 EPA) shows what aggressive fronts can do.

concerns.title: Deep TDs outrunning deep efficiency
concerns.body: Three touchdowns on 29 deep attempts comes with a 20.7% completion rate, two interceptions and -0.202 EPA. The air-yard jump from last season is the price of those scores. The completion rate probably won't fall further, but the touchdown rate on that few completions is the likeliest part of his line to regress.

trend.note: EPA went -7.8, -21.4, +8.5, +2.4. The last two games brought 591 yards and six scores, but also three interceptions, seven sacks and worsening accuracy. Production is trending up while the process isn't.

nextGame.headline: Thinned Colts pass rush and a generous secondary set up volume.
nextGame.body:
Indianapolis is a defense he can work against. It ranks 22nd in EPA and 20th against the pass, and it has allowed 305.8 passing yards a game to quarterbacks, 31st in the league. Its 17th-ranked sack rate isn't the kind of rush that exposes his shotgun problems the way New England's blitz-heavy plan did. The Colts are also middling (21st) on short throws, which is exactly where Rodgers is efficient, so the quick game and middle-of-the-field throws to the tight ends should be there. Pittsburgh comes in on 10 days' rest after the Thursday game in Cleveland.

Availability tilts his way. Edge Arden Key (65% of snaps) is out and Micheal Clemons is on IR, which strips the Colts' pass rush further. On offense, Indianapolis is without Keenan Allen and Alec Pierce, which should blunt a passing game already ranked 30th in EPA and keep Pittsburgh's leaky deep defense from being tested much. The risk is game script: the Colts' run game ranks 1st in EPA and can shorten the game. On Rodgers' side, Rico Dowdle (42% of snaps) is uncertain with a toe injury. If he sits, Jaylen Warren carries more of the backfield, and the under-center play-action that has been Rodgers' best look loses a bit of punch.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Colts edge rush vs. his sacks
keyMatchups.body: With Key out, the Colts' rush loses its most-used edge. A defense with a 17th-ranked sack rate is a far cry from the 18-blitz plan that wrecked him in Week 2. Fewer drive-killing sacks on third down is the biggest swing in his efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game into soft underneath coverage
keyMatchups.body: Indianapolis ranks 21st against short passes, and Rodgers' short throws return +0.255 EPA. A heavy diet of tight end and Wilson targets is the efficient way to move the ball here.

keyMatchups.title: Colts ground game controlling clock
keyMatchups.body: The Colts' top-ranked rushing offense meets a Pittsburgh run defense ranked 20th. With Allen and Pierce out, Indianapolis has every reason to lean on the run, which could trim his possession count even in a favorable matchup.

nextGame.watch: How many of his dropbacks come from shotgun on third-and-long. If the Colts' thinned rush still gets home there, the favorable matchup on paper won't matter.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable: the staff is committed to passing, and he has played 96-100% of snaps every week. Expect yardage in the mid-200s with real week-to-week swings driven by opponent pass rush. The 4.6% TD rate is plausible but leans on deep scores that a 20.7% deep completion rate won't keep supporting, so touchdowns should drift down a little while interceptions hold near one every 40 attempts. Efficiency is unlikely to improve much given three seasons of decline and a rising bad-throw rate. The best case is a creep toward his 2024-25 EPA levels, near average, as the schedule softens.

The lever is play design more than Rodgers himself. More under-center play-action and middle-of-the-field targets to the tight ends and Wilson would raise his floor. A pass rate this far over expected, in an offense whose run game is its strength, drags his efficiency down while it props up his raw totals.
swingFactors: Opponent pass rush and blitz rate on third down
Whether the deep-shot touchdowns keep coming at a 20% completion rate
Run-game health (Dowdle) and how much under-center play-action stays in the plan

bets.reason: The Colts have allowed 305.8 passing yards a game to QBs (31st) and are missing their most-used edge rusher, while Pittsburgh passes at the 3rd-highest rate over expected. The main risk is the Colts' top-ranked run game shortening the game.

Pittsburgh's defense (13th in EPA) faces a Colts passing offense ranked 30th and now without Allen and Pierce, and the Steelers come in on 10 days' rest. Rodgers' inefficiency keeps the margin from being comfortable.
Both offenses rank 24th-25th in EPA, and Pittsburgh's four games have averaged 41 combined points. The injury-depleted Colts passing game points toward a run-heavy, clock-draining script.

confidence.note: Only four games and small splits, but the efficiency decline matches three seasons of career data.
